newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Softer euro makes no sense - central bank source.
newsitem.headline: Softer euro makes no sense - central bank source.

text.p: A senior source at a European central bank on Monday brushed off talk European policy makers were interested in a softer euro, saying this made no sense.
"All this talk of a softer euro is not common sense," the source said on the fringes of the Bank for International Settlements annual meeting.
The source added no central bank or government "in the world is playing the game of a weak currency."
Looking ahead, the source said the stability pact would only be enhanced, but not in any way watered down if any changes were made at all.
The stability pact, brainchild of German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, was designed to ensure stable fiscal policies among nations participating in the single currency area after 1999.
Officials in France have suggested they would like to alter the pact ahead of its formal approval by European leaders later this month.
"The stability pact is important and would only be enriched," the source said when asked about the possability of changes to the agreement.
The source also said "the credibility of the euro is absolutely essential."
